books.section: Topic 5.9 Government Policies During the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Frederick Douglass, “Men of Color, to Arms!” (March 1863)

stimulus.source_note: Frederick Douglass, “Men of Color, to Arms!”, speech delivered March 2, 1863, Rochester, New York, published March 21, 1863. Public domain. Wording verified against the BlackPast and National Park Service texts. “. . .” marks omitted text between passages, quoted in their order in the source.
stimulus.text:
“When first the rebel cannon shattered the walls of Sumter and drove away its starving garrison, I predicted that the war then and there inaugurated would not be fought out entirely by white men. . . . Liberty won by white men would lose half its luster. ‘Who would be free themselves must strike the blow.’ ‘Better even die free, than to live slaves.’”

—Frederick Douglass, “Men of Color, to Arms!”, speech in Rochester, New York, March 2, 1863

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: Douglass argues that the war “would not be fought out entirely by white men.” His main point is that

options.text: white soldiers should refuse to fight.
options.misconception: Background: Douglass urges Black men to join the fight, not white soldiers to refuse it.

options.text: the war should end at once by negotiation.
options.misconception: Background: Douglass urges Black men to take up arms, not to negotiate an end to the war.

options.text: Black men should wait until the war ends.
options.misconception: Background: Douglass says now is the time to strike, not to wait until after the war.

options.text: Black men should enlist and fight for the Union.

rationales.A: Background: Douglass urges Black men to join the fight, not white soldiers to refuse it.
rationales.B: Background: Douglass urges Black men to take up arms, not to negotiate an end to the war.
rationales.C: Background: Douglass says now is the time to strike, not to wait until after the war.
rationales.D: Douglass predicts the war will not be fought out entirely by white men, and he calls Black men to arms.
rationales.general:
1. Douglass opens with a prediction made at Sumter: this war will need Black soldiers.
2. Two years of war have proved him right.
3. His call is direct: take up arms now.
4. The war is the moment to claim freedom by fighting for it.
Remember: a call to arms is an argument that freedom is won, not waited for.
